name: Kara-Keche Pass
near: The Kara-Keche coal miners’ settlement (open pit, ~3.6 km as the crow flies, ~2,800 m); the nearest village in the valley is Bash-Kuugandy (Bashkaingdy) at the mouth of the gorge: from there it is 75 km of dirt road to Song-Kol (dangerousroads, Too.kg). The district centre is Chayek.
elev: 3,384 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan, OunTravela, dangerousroads, quad-offroad); other sources: 3,364 m (Nomad's Land), 3,348 m (Too.kg), ~3,350 m (Baibol).
short: The south-western road pass (about 3,384 m) from the Jumgal valley to Lake Song-Kol — through a gorge with red cliffs and the country’s largest coal open pit.
desc: Kara-Keche is a pass in the Moldo-Too mountains separating the Jumgal valley from the Song-Kol basin. The road climbs through the 50-km Kara-Keche gorge, where reddish rock slopes contrast with spruce groves; at about 2,800 m there is an open coal pit, the largest coal deposit in Kyrgyzstan, with a small blue lake in the spoil heap. Thanks to the pit the dirt road is kept passable, but heavy coal trucks use it constantly. From the saddle you get a view of Song-Kol and of the gorge. The pass is popular with cyclists and off-road drivers; Nomad's Land calls it the most car-accessible pass to Song-Kol, and OunTravela calls it stony but well kept.
guide: Use Kara-Keche if you are heading to Song-Kol from the west — from Suusamyr, Chayek or the Kyzyl-Korgon canyons: it is the most logical route and ties the lake and the Jumgal valley into one loop. On the climb, stop at the viewpoint above the coal pit — the little blue lake among the black spoil heaps looks unexpected. From the saddle Song-Kol is the first thing to open up — the best shot is in clear weather before noon. Let the coal “Shacman” trucks pass at narrow spots and do not stand in the cloud of dust behind them. Do not drink river water below the pit — take it from springs.
see: The panorama of Song-Kol from the saddle; the Kara-Keche gorge with red cliffs and spruce groves; the open coal pit with the blue lake on the spoil heap; the jailoo (summer pasture) on the south-western shore of Song-Kol; in the valley — Jumgal and the Kyzyl-Korgon canyons.
skip: You are going to Song-Kol from Kochkor — Kalmak-Ashuu is much closer. You dislike dust and heavy truck traffic on a narrow dirt road. You want a beautiful serpentine for its own sake — Moldo-Ashuu is more spectacular.
diff: Moderate for a driver: a stony but maintained dirt road (OunTravela), a climb to ~3,384 m, heavy truck traffic. TripAdvisor: “quite a normal road”, but a 4×4 is needed. For cyclists — a long climb (used on bike tours).
when: Late June — September. All passes to Song-Kol are blocked by snow until June (OunTravela); TripAdvisor notes Kara-Keche as one of the last passes to open. Safe from June to September (dangerousroads); snow lies at Song-Kol for 180–200 days a year.
hours: An open road with no barriers; the coal miners use it year-round up to the pit (~2,800 m), but the section over the saddle to Song-Kol is closed by snow in winter and spring. There is no official schedule — ask drivers in Chayek/Kochkor.
daytime: Morning until noon: clear weather and a view of Song-Kol, fewer clouds; towards evening — thunderstorms and fog at altitude.
how: From the Jumgal valley (the Kochkor — Chayek — Suusamyr/Kazarman road): from the village of Bash-Kuugandy go south through the Kara-Keche gorge past the coal pit to the pass and on to the south-western shore of Song-Kol — about 75 km of dirt road in all (dangerousroads). Nomad's Land offers a Song-Kol — Kara-Keche — Kyzyl-Korgon route. The drive to Song-Kol over the pass takes 4–4.5 h (TripAdvisor review).
needcar: Yes: a 4×4 or a high-clearance crossover (OunTravela/TripAdvisor recommend a 4×4); there is no public transport over the pass. Alternatives are a bicycle or a horse route.
self: Yes, in your own 4×4; no permits. The road is easy to find — it follows the coal trucks up to the pit. Above the pit there are few people; at Song-Kol itself there are yurts in summer.
roadtype: Dirt/gravel from Bash-Kuugandy to Song-Kol (~75 km), stony but maintained because of the coal pit; coal grit and stones on the surface; heavy trucks. Above the pit to the saddle — a mountain dirt road with steep gradients (OunTravela).
traveltime: Bash-Kuugandy — Song-Kol over the pass: 4–4.5 h (TripAdvisor). From Bishkek to Chayek ~5–6 h (estimate); Bishkek — Song-Kol via Kara-Keche is a long day.
stay: There are no cafes, shops or hotels in the gorge (Too.kg); plenty of spots for a tent, and springs. The nearest overnights are yurt camps on the south-western and southern shores of Song-Kol (budget $10–25 with meals, 2025–2026) and guesthouses in Chayek/the Jumgal valley (prices not confirmed).
net: There is mobile coverage in the Kara-Keche gorge (Too.kg, 2023 — probably from the coal pit’s towers); the operator is not stated. On the saddle and at Song-Kol the signal is unstable or absent.
entry: Free: no fees for driving over the pass are mentioned in any source.
transfer: No published prices for a 4×4 specifically via Kara-Keche were found. A guide for Song-Kol: 2,500–3,500 som per car from Kochkor (visitkyrgyzstan.org); the Bishkek — Kochkor marshrutka (minibus) 350 som (May 2026).
bring: A warm jacket and hat (snow is possible at 3,384 m in summer), a spare tyre, spring water or a supply (river water below the pit is unfit — Too.kg), a mask/buff against coal dust, cash, offline maps.
warn: Heavy coal-truck traffic: dust, narrow spots, stones on the road. Do not drink river water below the pit. The pass is one of the last to open (snow until June). Weather at altitude changes fast — fog and snow are possible in summer.
food: There are no eateries on the pass. In Song-Kol yurts — kumys, beshbarmak, boorsok, kaymak; in Chayek — roadside cafes (lagman, manty). Dishes at specific places were not checked.
reviews: Google Maps: 4/5, 12 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor (Kara-Keche Pass): 4.4/5, 7 reviews (2015 — February 2020; viewed 07.10.2026). Pros: stunning views in clear weather, an alternative route to Song-Kol from Jumgal. Cons: the coal pit and trucks, the pass opens late, little public transport.
p.sum: Kara-Keche is the north-western “gateway” to Song-Kol from the Jumgal valley: from the village of Bash-Kuugandy (Chayek area) ≈75 km of gravel past the coal pit to the south-western shore, 4–4.5 h, best in a 4×4. Open from late June to September. IMPORTANT: on 3 July 2026 a mudflow destroyed a bridge at km 30–32 of the Dyikan — Kara-Keche — Moldo-Ashuu road, and passage was fully closed with no restoration date — check the status before the trip (Kyrgyzkomur, local drivers). It makes the most sense to use the pass on the way out from Song-Kol to the Kyzyl-Korgon canyons and Suusamyr.
p.apps.0.title: From the north: Chayek/Bash-Kuugandy → Kara-Keche gorge → pass → Song-Kol
p.apps.0.from: Chayek (Jumgal district); Bishkek ≈5–6 h to Chayek; Kochkor → Chayek via the Kyzart pass
p.apps.0.route: Bishkek → Balykchy → Kochkor → Kyzart pass → Chayek/Dyikan → Bash-Kuugandy → Kara-Keche gorge (≈50 km) → coal pit (≈2,800 m) → pass (≈3,350–3,384 m) → south-western shore of Song-Kol
p.apps.0.km: ≈75 km of dirt road from Bash-Kuugandy to Song-Kol; the climb through the gorge is ≈37 km with ≈1,200 m of elevation gain (Komoot)
p.apps.0.time: 4–4.5 h from Bash-Kuugandy to the lake
p.apps.0.surface: Gravel/dirt, maintained for the sake of the pit, but with sandy sections (cyclists complain about a “very sandy” road), coal dust, steep gradients above the pit. There is no paved road, although some maps show one
p.apps.0.season: Late June — September; one of the last passes to open. In summer 2026 — risk of mudflows (bridge destroyed 03.07.2026)
p.apps.0.last: Chayek — the last fuel stations, shops, ATM (ATM availability not confirmed in sources); in the gorge there are no shops or cafes, coverage is partial
p.apps.0.parking.d: No dedicated parking; stop on the roadside at viewpoints on the saddle
p.apps.0.haz: Mudflows and a destroyed bridge (07.2026), heavy coal KamAZ trucks, a polluted river (do not drink the water), snow/fog on the saddle
p.apps.1.title: From the south: from Song-Kol (south-western shore) down into Jumgal
p.apps.1.route: South-western shore → Kara-Keche pass → pit → Bash-Kuugandy → Jumgal valley → Kyzyl-Korgon/Suusamyr or Kochkor
p.apps.1.surface: Same; the descent is long and dusty
p.apps.1.season: July — September is the most reliable
p.apps.1.last: There are no services at Song-Kol — fill up in advance in Kochkor/Naryn
p.apps.1.haz: Do not drive into the Batay-Aral area on the south-west of the lake, fenced off since 09.2026

p.transport.0.details: Departs early in the morning when full

p.transport.1.price: a guide — 4×4 Kochkor — Song-Kol ≈5,200 som per car (2026)
p.transport.2.details: Multi-day routes including the Kara-Keche crossing

p.iti.0.title: Transit Song-Kol → Kyzyl-Korgon
p.iti.0.plan: Morning at Song-Kol → 9:00 depart → 13:00 Bash-Kuugandy → lunch in Chayek → Kyzyl-Korgon canyons by evening → night in a tent at Kokomeren or Kyzyl-Oi → Suusamyr → Bishkek.
p.iti.1.title: 3-day loop
p.iti.1.plan: Bishkek → Kochkor → Kalmak-Ashuu → Song-Kol (night) → Kara-Keche → Jumgal → Kyzyl-Oi (night) → Suusamyr → Bishkek.
p.season: June: often still closed by snow. July — September: passable, but summer downpours cause mudflows (bridge destroyed 03.07.2026). October — May: closed to tourists.
p.budget.economy: Without your own car, crossing Kara-Keche is not economical: only a 4×4 rental (≈5,000+ som per car) + a yurt for 1,000–2,000 som.
p.budget.comfort: 4×4 tour/car with driver around the Song-Kol loop: €120–$650 for 2 days (Tripster tours).
p.permits: Not required; no fees. Passage restrictions by Kyrgyzkomur are possible in case of accidents on the road.
p.access: By car only; for children and older people it is a long dusty drive with no services. Wheelchair users — view it from the car.
